summary: This week in AI news, several significant developments emerged. Anthropic introduced watermarks for its AI models, while Spotify began labeling 'AI Persona' profiles. OpenAI launched a ChatGPT desktop app for Linux and started testing ads in ChatGPT. Google's Gemini app surged to 1 billion users, and NVIDIA announced partnerships to establish independent financing platforms for AI factory compute.
insight: The increasing focus on watermarking AI-generated content and the introduction of ads in ChatGPT signal a shift towards greater transparency and monetization in the AI industry, as companies strive to balance the benefits of AI with the need for accountability and revenue streams.
highlights: Anthropic's new watermarking system aims to identify AI-generated text, addressing concerns about AI misuse.
Spotify's 'AI Persona' labels will help distinguish between human and AI-generated music, impacting music recommendations.
OpenAI's ChatGPT desktop app for Linux expands access to AI capabilities, while the introduction of ads in ChatGPT marks a new revenue stream.
